newsitem.title: UK: Cadbury profits up, mulls acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Cadbury profits up, mulls acquisitions.

text.p: British sweets and soft drinks group Cadbury Schweppes Plc reported a 16 percent increase in annual profits Wednesday and said it might hit the acquisition trail using cash from the sale of its stake in Coca-Cola & Schweppes Beverages.
The company said strong performances from both confectionery and beverages helped to drive up profits, which were at the top of market expectations.

Pretax profits rose to 592 million pounds ($955 million) from 511 million ($824 million), on sales of 5.12 billion pounds ($8.26 billion), up from 4.78 billion pounds ($7.71 billion). The dividend was increased by 6 percent to 17 pence a share (27 cents).
Chief Executive John Sunderland said the group had performed strongly across the whole range of the group's businesses.
"We regard it as a strong year. It's good for us that it's across both our beverages and our confectionery businesses and most of our markets performed very well," he said in an interview.

Sunderland said Cadbury would look at the possibility of making acquisitions using the 623 million pound ($1 billion) proceeds from the sale of its 51 percent share in Coca-Cola & Schweppes Beverages completed last month.

The money would give Cadbury lots of options to develop its brands both in soft drinks and confectionery. The company could also "acquire any appropriate businesses that we see, be it in beverages or I guess more likely in confectionery," he said.

In soft drinks in North America, Dr Pepper achieved 4 percent growth by volume and its overall growth outpaced the market as it has done for the last decade. But Sunderland acknowledged that competition was fierce. Cadbury's 7 Up was only now stabilising after many years of decline.
European soft drinks suffered from a poor summer in northern Europe, with most markets flat or down.

In Britain, the soft drink market was down slightly against the very hot summer in 1995. But Coca Cola & Schweppes Beverages profits were up 3 percent, which Cadbury considered very satisfactory give the outstanding summer in 1995.
In confectionery, all Cadbury's core companies had a good year. In Britain, Cadbury Ltd. increased market share for the third year in a row, driven by product innovation.
Fuse, launched in September, was in the top three selling chocolate bar brands in Britain along with Mars and Kitkat, Sunderland said.
